worker_notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Dissonance Arousal: Physiological Evidence, Robert T. Croyle and Joel Cooper, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1983, Vol. 45, No. 4, 782-791; its provenance header gives DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.45.4.782. This matches the assigned original reference. It contains a primary empirical report, including both experiments, methods, results, discussion and references, across pp. 782-791. No PDF was supplied. Target determined from Experiment 1, the induced-compliance attitude-change outcome and page-5 locator, independently of numeric matching. Retained printed F statistic (canonical OCR uses lowercase l for numerator df); no metric conversion. Same-test p < .01 preserved. Candidate N = 30 participants from Method; statement that an attitude change score was calculated for each subject is suggestive, but no explicit final analytic count accompanies the contrast. N is left null rather than inferred from df or equated automatically to participation. No N arithmetic performed. Other page-5 tests are the choice manipulation check (F( 1,27) = 50.17, p < .01), attitude premeasure (F(2,27) < 1), and contrast between nondissonance cells (F(2,27) < 1); their outcomes differ from the focal induced-compliance attitude-change prediction. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
